title: Commodity Manager - Liquid Nitrogen Cooling System
description:
WHY VEIR?

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts, VEIR is a U.S.-based designer and manufacturer of category-defining superconducting power delivery systems built for the extreme energy demands of the AI era. By commercializing next-generation superconducting technology into deployable, real-world systems, VEIR delivers ~10× higher power density than conventional options, enabling “speed-to-power” where incremental optimization falls short. VEIR’s initial focus is AI data centers behind the meter, with solutions engineered for repeatable deployment through reference designs and integrated controls, designed to incorporate learnings as deployments scale.

The Role

VEIR is seeking a Commodity Manager to own sourcing and supplier management for the Liquid Nitrogen (LIN) Cooling System — a technically demanding, cryogenics-driven subsystem with long-lead, often sole-sourced components that are critical to product reliability.

This person will run the sourcing program for the cooling system, focused on reducing long lead times through multi-sourcing strategy, supplier development, and supplier agreements. As part of VEIR’s NPI stage-gate process, this role owns key sourcing deliverables at each phase — candidate identification, RFI/RFQ development with Engineering, supplier audits, PPAP quality support, and process validation — to move cooling system suppliers from qualification through production readiness. This role requires close collaboration with Engineering and Quality on supplier qualification — including site audits — as well as cross-functional coordination across Product, Commercial, Project, Finance, Procurement, and Logistics teams.

In the first 3 months you'll

  • Learn VEIR’s LIN cooling system architecture, current supplier base, and known lead time/capacity constraints.
  • Build relationships with key cooling system suppliers, including pump, skid, and vessel fabricators.
  • Support ongoing supplier development activities aimed at reducing long lead times on critical components, working toward 4–5 commercially viable candidates per critical component.
  • Partner with Engineering to support internal RFI development and preliminary RFQs against early (Ph2/Ph3) BOM, drawing, and specification releases.
  • Partner with Procurement on AVL status and onboarding documentation for cooling system suppliers.
  • Join Engineering and Quality on at least one supplier site visit or technical/quality capability audit to build first-hand supplier knowledge.

In the first 6 months you'll

  • Own the sourcing strategy and supplier base for the LIN Cooling System commodity, including pumps, skids, vessels, and related cryogenic components.
  • Own development of detailed production RFQs following design release, incorporating manufacturing requirements, critical-to-quality (CTQ) specs, and PPAP/qualification requirements, in partnership with Engineering.
  • Support Engineering during sample builds and DFM iteration with candidate suppliers, ensuring feedback closes into the design ahead of design lock.
  • Partner with Quality to support supplier PPAP submissions (Part Submission Warrant, dimensional reports, process capability, material certifications) as part of production qualification.
  • Support process validation / run-at-rate studies to confirm supplier capacity and process capability against forecast.
  • Drive multi-sourcing strategy and supplier capacity development to reduce long lead times on critical components, and support second-source qualification for the highest-risk items.
  • Identify, evaluate, and qualify fabricators or contract manufacturers to support cooling system components as VEIR scales.
  • Lead negotiation of supplier agreements, pricing structures, and commercial terms in partnership with Procurement and Finance.
  • Build supplier scorecards and support periodic business reviews as suppliers move into ramp.
  • Partner with Logistics on packaging and shipping plans, including any special handling requirements for cooling system components.
  • Build a multi-year sourcing roadmap for the LIN Cooling System commodity in support of VEIR’s scale-up plans.

To be successful in this role

You Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in supply chain, commodity management, or strategic sourcing, ideally within a technical or cryogenics-adjacent environment.
  • A technical engineering background; experience in cryogenics preferred.
  • Experience setting up or managing fabricators or contract manufacturers preferred.
  • Experience developing RFIs and RFQs in partnership with engineering teams, from prototype-level through production-intent sourcing.
  • Familiarity with NPI stage-gate processes and PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) is strongly preferred.
  • Experience negotiating supplier agreements and multi-sourcing strategies, particularly for long-lead-time components.
  • Comfort conducting supplier site audits and working closely with Quality and Engineering to assess manufacturing capability.
  • Experience in a hardware, hard tech, or manufacturing environment; startup or scale-up experience is a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical field preferred.
  • Willingness to travel for supplier visits, audits, and qualification activities.

You Are

  • Comfortable owning a technically complex commodity with long lead times and limited supplier options.
  • A relationship builder who earns supplier trust while holding a firm line on cost, quality, and delivery.
  • Structured and proactive — you build sourcing roadmaps rather than reacting to the next fire.
  • A strong cross-functional collaborator across Product, Commercial, Engineering, and Finance.

title: Director of Manufacturing Quality Operations
description:
WHY VEIR?

Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Woburn, Massachusetts, VEIR is a U.S.-based designer and manufacturer of category-defining superconducting power delivery systems built for the extreme energy demands of the AI era. By commercializing next-generation superconducting technology into deployable, real-world systems, VEIR delivers ~10× higher power density than conventional options, enabling “speed-to-power” where incremental optimization falls short. VEIR’s initial focus is AI data centers behind the meter, with solutions engineered for repeatable deployment through reference designs and integrated controls, designed to incorporate learnings as deployments scale.

The Role
We are building the manufacturing and quality foundation for a new class of critical infrastructure products — including a liquid nitrogen (LIN) cooling system and a termination assembly — that will support live data center deployments. We are looking for a Director of Manufacturing & Quality Operations to lead this foundation from the ground up: taking our products through pilot builds in 2027 and into a manufacturing and quality system capable of scaling quickly to support live data centers in 2028.

This leader will manage two functions — Manufacturing Engineering and Quality — and will be a critical voice in building the operational credibility our customers need to trust us with mission-critical infrastructure. This role reports to the COO and works in close partnership with our internal design engineering team and our Cable Manufacturing team (a peer function producing cable assemblies in-house, which does not report into this role but is a close collaborator).

What You'll Own

Manufacturing Engineering

  • Directly manage the Sr. Manufacturing Engineer – Termination Assemblies and the Manufacturing Engineer – LIN System, and grow the team as volume scales.
  • Drive Design for Manufacturability/Assembly (DFM/DFA) across both product lines in full partnership with our internal design engineering team, optimizing for lead time, cost, and quality.
  • Own the fabricator and contract manufacturer relationships for both product lines — sourcing, qualifying, and managing partners, and acting as a ruthless advocate for our cost, quality, and schedule requirements.
  • Bring in outside technical experts as needed (e.g., cryogenics, welding/pressure vessel, high-power termination, controls integration) to close capability gaps and de-risk critical design and process decisions.
  • Own the manufacturing readiness roadmap: successful pilot builds in 2027, transitioning to a production-ready design and supply base that can support live data center deployments in 2028.
  • Build a scaling plan (supplier capacity commitments, second-source strategies, tooling/fixturing investment) so the organization can flex production up quickly if order volume accelerates.
  • Serve as a technical and operational reference point for prospective customers evaluating our manufacturing readiness and reliability.

Quality

Quality is being built as a company-wide operating discipline, not a back-office function — held to the same bar our own customers apply to their suppliers, and built with the same resilience mindset large infrastructure OEMs now expect across their supply base. This role builds and leads three areas, phased as follows:

Phase 1 – Quality Management System

  • Design and stand up the company's Quality Management System from the ground up: a documented quality plan, defined control systems and written procedures for each quality function, and the traceability discipline (serial/lot tracking, calibration records, inspection and test records) needed to withstand external audit.
  • Establish document and revision control so engineering, quality, and manufacturing always work from the current released specification, including a formal process for reviewing, approving, and time/quantity-bounding any deviation from drawing or spec.
  • Lead the organization through ISO 9001 certification for manufacturing operations by Q3 2027, establishing the quality management foundation and audit-ready documentation this requires.
  • Define and own the longer-term roadmap to extend ISO 9001 certification company-wide, positioning us as a certified product developer and a credible, audit-ready partner as we scale toward production — a bar increasingly expected by OEMs and infrastructure customers of their suppliers and partners.

Phase 2 – Supplier Quality

  • Hire and build the Supplier Quality Engineering function and stand up a formal supplier approval process: preliminary supplier assessment, an audited quality-system review scored against a standardized checklist, prototype/technical approval, a process audit during sample production, and a signed quality agreement (defining acceptable quality levels and non-quality cost recovery) before any supplier ships production volume.
  • Scale part-approval rigor— dimensional data, process flow, manufacturing/assembly instructions, control plans, measurement system analysis, capability studies, and agency compliance documentation — with the highest bar applied to new, custom-designed assemblies such as cryogenic pressure components and high-power terminations.
  • Run ongoing supplier performance management: monthly scorecards against defined targets (defective PPM, on-time delivery, order acknowledgment time, corrective-action response time, RMA turnaround), regular supplier business reviews, and a structured corrective action process — rapid containment, documented root cause, and verified permanent corrective action on a defined timeline — with the goal of zero defects shipped in the finished system.
  • Build supply chain resilience into the supplier base, not just compliance: map critical suppliers and their sub-suppliers (second-tier visibility), flag single-source and geopolitical exposure, and score bill-of-materials risk by sourcing method, supplier risk, and technical criticality so issues are caught and mitigated before they become a shipment delay or field failure.
  • Own supplier compliance and disclosure requirements as they apply to our products and customers (e.g., material certifications, agency/regulatory compliance, conflict minerals and environmental/sustainability disclosures), building the reporting discipline our customers will expect us to demonstrate in turn.

Phase 3 – Customer Quality

  • Hire a Customer Quality Engineer and build the customer-facing quality system: a documented plan for resolving warranty and field quality issues (expedited replacement material, field rework procedures, on-site support), customer complaint intake and corrective-action reporting, and a cadence of customer quality/business reviews.
  • Ensure we can execute against whatever quality requirements our customers impose contractually — including customer-specific supplier quality manuals, audits, scorecards, and reporting obligations — with the same discipline and rigor we require of our own supply base.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner closely with the Cable Manufacturing team lead to ensure end-to-end system quality and coordinated manufacturing planning, even though that team does not report into this role.
  • Represent manufacturing and quality readiness to leadership, investors, and prospective customers.
  • Build a repeatable, systematic approach to risk management across manufacturing and supply chain — treating it as an ongoing discipline rather than a one-time setup.

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations and/or quality leadership for complex electromechanical, high-power, or critical infrastructure hardware.
  • Direct experience building a manufacturing engineering and/or quality function from the ground up — startup, new product line, or early-stage manufacturing scale-up experience strongly preferred.
  • People-management experience leading manufacturing and/or quality engineers.
  • Deep working knowledge of DFM/DFA, contract manufacturer/fabricator management, incoming and first-article inspection processes (e.g., PPAP), and supplier corrective action systems.
  • Experience standing up a Quality Management System and leading an organization through ISO 9001 (or equivalent) certification.
  • Experience building supplier quality programs end-to-end: supplier approval/audit methodology, PPAP or equivalent first-article discipline, performance scorecards, and structured corrective action (8D or similar).
  • Experience building supply chain risk visibility (critical/single-source supplier mapping, sub-supplier exposure, bill-of-materials risk scoring) as a proactive discipline rather than a reactive one.
  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity at an early stage — able to build scalable systems while staying hands-on with day-to-day execution.
  • Strong cross-functional collaborator, especially with design/product engineering teams.
  • Excellent communicator, able to represent the company's operational and quality credibility directly to customers and partners.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with cryogenic systems, pressure vessels, or high-power electrical termination/connection hardware.

  • Own end-to-end delivery of assigned products through PDP Phases 0–6: ideation, requirements and concept design, preliminary design and prototype testing, detailed design and integrated system testing, product launch and manufacturing readiness, at-scale production and sustain, and deprecation.

As Senior Technical Product Manager – Cable Systems at VEIR, you will serve as the single-threaded owner for VEIR's cable systems product area, with full accountability for product strategy, technical requirements, NPI execution, and commercial readiness across VEIR's low-voltage and medium-voltage cable assemblies. This role is deeply technical and hardware-focused, sitting at the intersection of electrical engineering, systems architecture, customer requirements, and commercial deployment.

You will translate data center power delivery requirements, including fault current ratings, voltage drop budgets, voltage ripple specifications, and AC/DC architecture needs into precise, testable product specifications. You will negotiate those requirements with engineering, drive them through NPI stage gates, and ensure VEIR's cable systems achieve certification, reliability, and manufacturability targets on the path to commercial deployment.

This is the right role for a technically rigorous product manager who has deep experience with low-voltage power distribution hardware, understands the data center power electronics ecosystem, and is energized by the challenge of bringing first-of-kind power delivery products to market.

In the first 3 months you'll

  • Ramp up on VEIR's cable systems architecture, including system interfaces, installation methods, performance requirements, LV power distribution topology, and data center application use cases.
  • Develop deep familiarity with VEIR's existing cable specifications, design tradeoffs, and constraints across conductor types, connectors, busbars, and insulation systems.
  • Conduct voice-of-customer (VoC) discovery with data center operators, electrical contractors, and internal applications and commercial teams to validate cable system requirements and pain points.
  • Perform competitive and ecosystem analysis of the data center power electronics landscape, including LV distribution equipment suppliers (busbars, cable conductors, switchgear) and key industry players.
  • Create initial product strategy and business case documents covering target use cases, technical requirements, cost targets, pricing assumptions, and certification obligations.

In the first 6 months you'll

  • Own and maintain product requirements and specifications for VEIR's cable systems, defining fault current ratings, voltage drop budgets, ripple limits, connector interface requirements, and applicable compliance standards (UL, NEC, IEC, IEEE).
  • Lead NPI stage-gate execution for cable systems products, ensuring designs progress from concept through prototype, validation, and commercial readiness, actively negotiating requirements and tradeoffs with engineering.
  • Partner closely with electrical, mechanical, systems, and manufacturing teams to ensure cable designs are optimized for performance, reliability, scalability, supply chain availability, and field installation.
  • Drive UL and relevant certification activities for cable systems products, working with engineering and third-party test labs to plan, execute, and document certification programs.
  • Serve as the technical product expert for commercial and applications teams, supporting customer conversations, technical evaluations, and early pilot deployments.

By the end of the first year you will have

  • Defined and executed the product roadmap for VEIR's cable systems portfolio, balancing near-term pilot delivery commitments with longer-term platform evolution toward medium-voltage capability.
  • Successfully driven one or more cable systems products through launch or pilot deployment, meeting MVP performance, cost, certification, and reliability targets.
  • Established clear, differentiated value propositions for VEIR's cable systems versus conventional alternatives in the data center power delivery market.
  • Developed and maintained technical product collateral including specification sheets, installation guides, compliance documentation, and sales enablement materials.
  • Acted as the cross-functional product leader, aligning engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and commercial teams around shared cable systems priorities and milestones.

To be successful in this role

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering required; advanced degree a plus.
  • 5–10 years of combined experience in electrical engineering and hardware product management, with direct experience in power electronics or low-voltage power distribution systems.
  • Deep, hands-on knowledge of low-voltage power distribution hardware, including cable conductors, busbars, and connectors is required; medium-voltage experience strongly desirable.
  • Strong understanding of AC/DC electrical architectures used in data center power delivery, including distribution topologies, switchgear integration, and server rack power paths.
  • Strong command of the data center power electronics ecosystem, including familiarity with major suppliers and the competitive landscape across LV distribution equipment.
  • Demonstrated experience defining and negotiating technical requirements and product specifications for NPI power electronics products, including fault current ratings, voltage drops, ripple specifications, and porting and connection interface requirements.
  • Hands-on experience managing NPI stage-gate lifecycles for physical hardware, from early concept through commercial launch.
  • Direct experience leading or supporting UL certification programs for power electronics or LV electrical hardware; familiarity with NEC and IEC standards.
  • Experience translating customer and application requirements into clear, testable product specifications in collaboration with engineering teams.
  • Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to drive alignment across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and commercial stakeholders.
  • Data center industry experience highly desirable.

  • Technically rigorous. You go deep on the engineering details, can hold your own in specification reviews, and know how to push back constructively when requirements need to evolve.
